_doc: The 21 groups of the town and buildings evidence pass (OA10) with the structures each one works. Generated by tools/bt/town/assign_groups.py from tools/bt/town/town_groups.py and the repository data; edit those, not this file. A building is worked in exactly one group: its primary group. Cross-references are in the evidence rows (field `see_also`).
assignment_rule: an id in `explicit` of town_groups.py goes to that group
a borough mass or a point inside the borough grid goes to the street group of the nearest street axis within 45 m, else the lanes group
a structure outside the borough goes to the area group of the nearest anchor (a gazetteer place or a curated farm key), whatever the distance (flag far_from_every_anchor when over 1500 m)
a building with a specialised group (church, college, seminary, railroad, tavern or hotel, mill or bridge, cemetery, public building) is worked there
street_axes_basis: eight street junctions of the Hopkins 1858 borough inset, docs/basemap1863/maps/gcps/hopkins_inset.json (fit 1.9 m, leave-one-out 2.9 m); the axes are straight lines through them, extended; a rule for grouping, not a survey

groups_list.title: Public and institutional buildings: court house, prison, almshouse, schools, banks, halls
groups_list.scope: The Adams County court house (record bld-courthouse; basemap STR-TOWN-COURTHOUSE, 2023 outline, error 8 m; the plan row says built 1858, Italianate, two storeys, about 70 ft clock tower, command post and hospital for both sides: every word of it rests on Wikipedia, a lead), the county prison, the almshouse complex north of the borough (basemap STR-ALMSHOUSE-COMPLEX_BUILDING1..9, nine Warren-plate symbols, error 45 m; the plan row says "no source retrieved"), public and private schools, banks, the post office, engine houses, market house and halls.

targets.name: Court House
targets.basis: record bld-courthouse; "Court House" counted in the 1863 papers

targets.name: Jail / prison
targets.basis: lead: "General Jail" and "Jail" occur in the 1863 papers (may be a county jail or a general term)

targets.name: Almshouse (county poorhouse) complex
targets.basis: basemap STR-ALMSHOUSE-COMPLEX_BUILDING1..9; PDF B.8.2 last row

targets.name: Banks
targets.basis: lead: "Brick Bank", "Bank" in the 1863 papers: which are Gettysburg banks is for the pass to read

issues: PDF rows rest on Wikipedia (lead): none of the court house particulars is documented until a local text carries it.
The 2023 outline of the court house is not the 1863 form unless a source says it is unchanged.
The almshouse complex is nine symbols with a 45 m error: the pass decides which symbols are almshouse buildings and which are not.

groups_list.title: Churches of the borough, their belfries and their use as hospitals
groups_list.scope: Presbyterian Church (record bld-presbyterian-church; basemap STR-TOWN-PRESBYTERIAN_CHURCH, error 40 m, confidence Contested; "208 Baltimore St"), Christ Lutheran Church (STR-TOWN-CHRIST_LUTHERAN, error 18 m; the basemap carries a street-number conflict, 30 versus 44 Chambersburg Street), St. Francis Xavier Catholic church (no geometry), the town church belfry used by snipers (no geometry), and every other church standing in July 1863 (Methodist, Reformed, African, others: the list is itself a finding of the pass: Hopkins 1858 inset, Jacobs 1864, the 1863 papers). Interiors changed for hospital use (pews removed, boards laid) belong to the building rows as states.

targets.name: Christ Lutheran Church
targets.basis: basemap STR-TOWN-CHRIST_LUTHERAN; "Lutheran Church" counted in the 1863 papers

targets.name: St. Francis Xavier Catholic church
targets.basis: record bld-st-francis-xavier; "Catholic Church" counted in the 1863 papers

targets.name: Other churches
targets.basis: to be found in the Hopkins inset legend and the 1863 papers; none is named here

issues: Presbyterian church site: the basemap confidence is Contested; the error bound is 40 m.
Christ Lutheran: 30 versus 44 Chambersburg Street in the sources of the basemap; the 1863 form of the church is unknown (2023 outline, error 18 m).
Every hospital-use row feeds the hospital pass (OA12, workstream bt-life-hospitals): rows carry the building id so the two passes meet.

groups_list.title: Pennsylvania College: Pennsylvania Hall and the other buildings of the campus
groups_list.scope: Pennsylvania Hall (record bld-pennsylvania-hall; basemap STR-TOWN-PENN_HALL, the main block of the 2023 outline, error 4 m, wings of 1889 left out; the plan row: designed 1835, built 1837-38, Greek Revival, four storeys, 150 x 45 ft, four-column south portico, cupola; signal officers June 30; hospital to about 29 July with about 700 casualties: every word from Wikipedia, a lead), the other campus buildings of 1863 (to be found: Hopkins inset, Jacobs 1864, the HABS record), the campus fences and grounds, and the photograph of Pennsylvania College of August 1863 (LOC 2014646151).

targets.name: Other college buildings of 1863
targets.basis: to be found in Jacobs 1864 (the author taught at the college) and the Hopkins inset

issues: The 2023 outline omits the wings of 1889 (basemap status main_block_drawn_wings_1889_omitted); the 1863 plan and form must come from HABS or a text that dates the wings.
The photograph of August 1863 is the best evidence of the 1863 appearance and is a picture: a reading of it is an observation row (evidence_kind image), never a measurement.

groups_list.title: The Lutheran Theological Seminary on Seminary Ridge and its neighbours: Schmucker Hall, Thompson house, Schultz house
groups_list.scope: Schmucker Hall ("Old Dorm"; record bld-schmucker-hall; STR-TOWN-SCHMUCKER_HALL, 2023 outline, error 4 m; cupola as observation post; hospital; about seven hundred patients: plan row, Wikipedia and other leads), the professors' houses and other seminary buildings of 1863 (to be found), the Thompson house (Lee's headquarters; record bld-thompson-house; STR-TOWN-THOMPSON_HOUSE), the Schultz house (STR-TOWN-SCHULTZ_HOUSE, named in the basemap as an Oak Ridge Academy building: to be checked) and the Sheads house (STR-TOWN-SHEADS_HOUSE, traced outline).
issues: The Brady "hole" in the cupola photograph is a negative defect, not damage (plan row); read it from the photograph itself, not from the plan.
The Thompson house: the plan row says the interior fire of 1896 is not the battle; a fence-burning statement (no date) is documented only by a lead.
Photograph 2018666299 ("G.J. White's house") has no stated place: do not assign it to a farm without a text that places it.

groups_list.title: The Gettysburg Railroad: depot, track, trestle, bridges and the unfinished grade with its cuts
groups_list.scope: The railroad station on Carlisle Street (record bld-rr-station; STR-TOWN-DEPOT, 2023 outline, error 6 m; RL-006 depot marker, error 15 m), the line of the Gettysburg Railroad (RL-001) and the unfinished grade west of the borough (RL-002, record P-12: the cut itself is part of the modern ground model), the Rock Creek trestle burned on 26 or 27 June (RL-007, record bld-rock-creek-rr-bridge), freight and engine buildings, culverts and bridges of the grade, the cuts and fills as they stood in 1863 (depth, length), the post-1863 lines never drawn (RL-003, RL-005, RL-004) and the unknown extent RL-002W.

targets.name: Unfinished railroad grade and its cuts
targets.basis: RL-002, record P-12; gazetteer "Railroad Cuts" (about 2.4 km west of the Diamond)

targets.name: Freight / engine buildings
targets.basis: lead: "Railroad Depot" counted in the 1863 papers; no other building is named

issues: Burned 26 versus 27 June (plan row: sources vary): carry both as a conflict, never one.
Traffic resumed 10 July per one passage and 1865 per another (plan row: internally inconsistent).
The depot of 2023 is altered (one-storey addition of 1886 per the plan row, Wikipedia): the 1863 form is not the 2023 outline.
Photograph 2018670663 shows Hanover Junction, not Gettysburg: it is context for burned bridges, not evidence for a Gettysburg building.
The Sanitary Commission offices (three photographs) stood somewhere near the depot: a place claim needs a text.

groups_list.title: Taverns, hotels and inns of the borough and the roads
groups_list.scope: Hotels of the borough in July 1863 (names counted in the 1863 papers: Globe Hotel, Eagle Hotel, Howard House, Mansion House, Clellan's Hotel; whether each is a Gettysburg hotel is for the pass to read), Black Horse Tavern on the Fairfield road (STR-TOWN-BLACK_HORSE_TAVERN, 2023 outline, error 8 m), Herr's Tavern (Warren label HERR TAVERN, two symbols), the Springs Hotel (Warren label SPRING, two symbols; the Park Service study "The Significance of the Harmon Farm and the Springs Hotel Woods"), the Dobbin House (STR-TOWN-DOBBIN_HOUSE, traced outline). A hotel on a borough street is worked here, not in the street group.

targets.name: Herr's Tavern
targets.basis: Warren plate labels at two symbols

issues: The basemap carries the Black Horse Tavern as a surviving building with a 2023 outline: its 1863 form is a question, not an answer.

groups_list.title: Mills, mill dams and bridges of Rock Creek, Willoughby Run, Stevens Run, Plum Run and Marsh Creek
groups_list.scope: McAllister's Mill (STR-SITE-MCALLISTER_MILL, named point, error 150 m: grist and saw mills with two dams), the Sachs mill and covered bridge on Marsh Creek (STR-SITE-SACHS_BRIDGE; outside the loaded ground), Hereter's mill (road RD-011), Horner's mill and the Rock Creek covered bridge of 1841 (plan B.8.4), and the bridges and fords of the basemap (BR-001..BR-015: BR-002 Baltimore Pike over Rock Creek, documented, error 70 m; BR-006 and BR-007 over Rock Creek; BR-011 and BR-015 on Willoughby Run; BR-004, BR-009, BR-013 over Stevens Run, open gaps; 11 outside the loaded ground), the Plum Run crossings (a plan gap) and the mill races and dams.

targets.name: Hereter's mill
targets.basis: road RD-011 "Hereter's Mill Road (Old Mill Road)"

targets.name: Horner's mill
targets.basis: plan B.8.4 row for the Taneytown Road

issues: Road-bridge widths and spans are open gaps in the plan; none is a generic number until the group REPORT names the generic rule.
The basemap bridge points carry 30 to 70 m error: a position row says so.

groups_list.title: Cemetery Hill: Evergreen Cemetery, the gatehouse and its pavilion, the walls and fences, other burial grounds
groups_list.scope: The Evergreen Cemetery gatehouse (record bld-evergreen-gatehouse; STR-TOWN-GATEHOUSE, 2023 outline, error 4 m, a right-side addition since; plan row: Italianate, finished November 1855, moderate damage on the evening of 2 July), the pavilion beside it (STR-TOWN-GATEHOUSE_PAVILION, photograph pose, lost), the cemetery fences and the monuments that stood in July 1863 (FEN-evergreen-cemetery, ENV-evergreen-cemetery), the stone walls of Cemetery Hill (P-02, P-03), brickyards and other buildings on the hill, and every other burial ground of the borough. The Soldiers' National Cemetery was laid out after the battle: it is recorded as a later feature and never drawn in the July scene.
issues: Photograph pose registers P03 and P26 (gatehouse) are "cannot judge": no camera position is documented; the 2023 outline merges the lodge and the pavilion.
The plan row for the gatehouse damage rests on Wikipedia and "NPS: moderate damage": the NPS text must be found in a local report.

groups_list.title: Baltimore Street from the Diamond to the cemetery gate
groups_list.scope: Every building on both sides of Baltimore Street south of the Diamond (the borough masses within 45 m of its axis, and the named houses: the McClellan house of Jennie Wade, 548 Baltimore Street, record bld-wade-house; the Garlach house; the Pierce house at Baltimore and Breckenridge; the Sweney, Rupp and McCreary houses; the Wills house, whose place is to be confirmed) and its fences. Churches, hotels, the court house and other specialised buildings on the street are worked in their own groups.

targets.name: Pierce house
targets.basis: record bld-pierce-house (PDF: corner Baltimore and Breckenridge)

targets.name: Sweney House, Rupp house, McCreary house
Wills house
targets.basis: part of record bld-poorhouse-christ-lutheran-wills: place and form to be found; assigned here pending the place

queries: gettysburg houses riddled shells baltimore street
issues: Borough masses (error 20 m) merge neighbouring buildings and may include buildings of 1863-69: an existence row for a mass is inferred at best and says which map shows it.
150+ bullet strikes on the Wade house are a plan count from Wikipedia: documented only from a local text.

groups_list.title: Chambersburg Street, west of the Diamond to the borough edge
groups_list.scope: Every building on both sides of Chambersburg Street from the Diamond to the west end of the borough (borough masses within 45 m of its axis; the Burns house, record bld-burns-house, razed after his death; the houses where first-day soldiers fought, sheltered or were wounded: to be found) and their fences. Christ Lutheran and any hotel on the street are worked in their own groups.
queries: gettysburg first day retreat through town
issues: The Burns house stood on Chambersburg Street per the plan row (Wikipedia, a lead): its place needs a text and a map reading.

groups_list.title: York Street (east of the Diamond) and Carlisle Street (north), with the Diamond
groups_list.scope: Every building on York Street from the Diamond to the east end of the borough and on Carlisle Street from the Diamond north (the borough masses within 45 m of either axis), the buildings facing the Diamond on the north and east, and their fences. The railroad station on Carlisle Street, the college and any hotel are worked in their own groups.
issues: The Diamond was a plain crossing in 1858 (basemap check against the Hopkins inset), a roundabout today: nothing drawn at the Diamond comes from the modern layout.

groups_list.title: Washington Street, Stratton Street and Breckenridge Street
groups_list.scope: Every building on Washington Street (west of Baltimore Street, the street the Taneytown Road enters), Stratton Street (east) and Breckenridge Street (the southern east-west street) within the borough grid, and their fences. The college campus and specialised buildings are worked in their own groups.
issues: Stratton Street runs east of Baltimore Street on the Hopkins inset control points: the group does not assume the modern street names for lanes beyond the eight junctions.

groups_list.title: West and East Middle Street, High Street, and the lanes and alleys of the borough
groups_list.scope: Every building on Middle Street and High Street (both halves) within the borough grid, every building on lanes and alleys (borough masses farther than 45 m from every named street axis), outbuildings, shops, stables and back lots, and their fences. The group also takes any borough mass the street groups cannot place.
issues: Lane and alley names are not in the repository (18 named lanes of the basemap have no traced line): names come only from a text.

groups_list.title: West of the borough: Seminary Ridge, McPherson Ridge, Herr Ridge and the Willoughby Run farms
groups_list.scope: The McPherson farm (record bld-mcpherson-farm; barn STR-MCPHERSON-BARN1 survives; farmhouse burned 1895 per the NPS; central wagon shed lost), the McMillan farm (STR-MCMILLAN-*), the Herbst woods and buildings (record bld-herbst), the farms along the Chambersburg Pike and the Hagerstown, Hereter's Mill and Black Horse Tavern roads (Warren labels: Herr, Leafer, Bender, Grist, Dustman, Tate, Kirk, Hoffman, Harman, Herbst, Plank, Currans and others), their fences (Thompson, McMillan, Seminary Ridge, Gamble's cavalry fence, McPherson / railroad-grade fences, Chambersburg Pike), the wall P-07 on Oak Ridge.

targets.name: McPherson farm (house, barn, wagon shed, orchard)
Farms named by the Warren plate west of the borough
targets.basis: symbol labels HERR, LEAFER, BENDER, GRIST, DUSTMAN, TATE, KIRK, HOFFMAN, HARMAN, PLANK, CURRANS (OCR hints)

issues: The McPherson barn did not burn on 1 July and the farmhouse burned in 1895 (plan, B.8.1 corrections): never draw a later event in the battle.
The Warren labels are OCR hints (HERBST, LEAFER, BENDER...): a name is used for a building only when a local text names the same occupant.

groups_list.title: North of the borough: Oak Ridge, Oak Hill, Blocher's Knoll, the Carlisle, Mummasburg and Harrisburg roads
groups_list.scope: The Forney, Hagy and McLean farms (basemap farm keys forney, hagy_beams, mclean), the Warren-plate farmsteads north of the borough (labels Blocher, Crawford, Kitsman, Josiah, Schaffer and others: OCR hints), the buildings of the first-day northern fight, and their fences and lanes.

targets.name: Blocher farm
targets.basis: Warren labels DAVID BLOCKER, JOHN BLOCKER (OCR hints)

issues: Many Warren symbols north and north-east of the borough are outside the loaded ground: they are worked here and flagged "beyond the ground", never dropped.

groups_list.title: East of Rock Creek: Benner's Hill, the Hanover Road, the York Pike, East Cavalry Field (Rummel)
groups_list.scope: The Rummel farm (record bld-rummel-farm: the barn survives, Stuart's men cut loopholes in the planking on 3 July; fences destroyed), the Benner, Wolf, Monfort, Mummard, Erbst, War and other farmsteads of the Warren plate east of the borough (OCR labels), the farm lanes and fences, and the farms along the Hunterstown and Low Dutch roads that stood within the battlefield of 3 July.

targets.name: Benner farm
targets.basis: Warren labels D. BENNER, BENNE (OCR hints); named in the task

issues: The Rummel loopholes (S-054) are documented only through Stone Sentinels (a lead): find the report or the NPS text.

groups_list.title: Culp's Hill, Spangler's Spring, Rock Creek and the Baltimore Pike east of Cemetery Hill (Culp, Spangler, Lady, Taney, Granite Schoolhouse)
groups_list.scope: The Henry Culp farm (record bld-henry-culp-farm; STR-CULP-*; five symbols, error 45 m), the George Spangler farm (the XI Corps hospital: record bld-spangler-farm; IDENTITY ISSUE TW-ID-01 below), the Granite Schoolhouse (record bld-granite-schoolhouse; razed 1921; no geometry), the Taney farm (record bld-taney-farm), the Daniel Lady farm (record bld-daniel-lady-farm: Confederate field hospital; plan row "documented (hospital); open gap (details)"), the Guinn farm (STR-LOST-GUINN_FARM), the Baltimore Pike farmsteads of the Warren plate (labels Signad, Ens, Pfeifer, Lightner, Cassalt, Heck, Wolf, Conover, Horn and others: OCR hints), the Rock Creek and White Run hospital complex (H-17) as buildings, the stone walls P-08, P-09 and the farm lanes.

targets.name: George Spangler farm (XI Corps hospital)
targets.basis: record bld-spangler-farm, plan row "Hospital Road"; NPS-SPANGLERS-SPRING

targets.name: Taney farm
targets.basis: record bld-taney-farm (shelled by 1st NY Battery M on 3 July per plan)

issues: TW-ID-01 (identity): the record bld-spangler-farm and hospital H-06 carry the details of George Spangler's farm (plan row: Hospital Road, 166 acres, XI Corps hospital, bank barn with 7 ft forebay); the product draws it on the geometry STR-SPANGLER_H-* which the NPS historical statement (NPS-HS-SPANGLER-HENRY, p.2, OCR text) places "between the Emmitsburg Road and Seminary Ridge", north of the Sherfy farm and south of the Codori farm, and the gazetteer "Spangler farm" lies there too. The two farms are different places. Neither reading is chosen here: the pass reads both farms from local texts and carries the identity as a selectable conflict (Law cl.6).
The Warren plate labels symbols near the Baltimore Pike "HENRY SPANGLER" (OCR hints, five symbols about 1.9 km south-east of the Diamond): the label does not decide which Spangler owned it in 1863.
anchors: Baltimore Pike, 1 mile east of Rock Creek

groups_list.title: Cemetery Ridge and the Taneytown Road: Leister, Hummelbaugh, Bryan, Biggs, Weikert, Frey, Patterson
groups_list.scope: The Leister house and barn (Meade headquarters; record bld-leister-house), the Hummelbaugh farm (II Corps hospital), the Bryan (Brien) farm, the Biggs house, the George and John Weikert farms (V Corps 2nd Division hospital), the Frey and Patterson farmsteads of the Warren plate, the Fisher log house, their fences and walls (Leister, Brian, the Cemetery Ridge walls, the Angle wall P-01, the Leister photograph wall P-13), and the Taneytown Road buildings south to the Round Tops.

targets.name: Bryan farm (house, barn, bake oven, second house)

issues: The Leister house of 1863 was two rooms of wood; the later two-storey addition is not 1863 (plan row; NPS).
The Bryan house and barn are reconstructions (plan row; NPS-BRYAN-HOUSE restoration report): reconstruction dimensions are not 1863 dimensions without a text that says so.
Photographs 2018666296 (Leister: "roughly" in the photo-match ledger) and 2018666298 (Bryan: cannot judge) are evidence for what is visible, never for a measurement.

groups_list.title: The Emmitsburg Road farms: Codori, Klingel, Rogers, Bliss, Sherfy, Wentz, Henry Spangler, Staub
groups_list.scope: The Codori farm (house of 1834 and brick addition of 1877, barn taken down 1882), the Klingel farm (log house; wounded sheltered; fences gone), the Rogers house (log; cellar used for wounded; torn down in the 1880s), the Bliss house and barn (burned on 3 July), the Sherfy house and barn (barn burned; orchard), the Wentz log house, the Henry Spangler farm (STR-SPANGLER_H-*: house, barn burned in the battle, smokehouse, stable; see TW-ID-01 in the Culp's Hill group), the Staub farm, the double post-and-rail fences of the road (FEN-emmitsburg-road, FEN-klingle, FEN-sherfy-orchard, FEN-warfield) and the walls P-10, P-11.
issues: TW-ID-01: see the Culp's Hill group: STR-SPANGLER_H-* is carried here as Henry Spangler's farm on the evidence of NPS-HS-SPANGLER-HENRY and the gazetteer; the hospital details of the plan row belong to the farm worked in farms-culps-hill-baltimore-pike.
Sherfy and Bliss fire times conflict (plan B.8.2; DD-PD rows): carry every reading, choose none.
The Codori barn of 1863 was smaller and was torn down in 1882: the basemap point is the barn "standing in 1868-69", not a documented 1863 footprint.

groups_list.title: Plum Run, the Wheatfield and the Round Tops: Trostle, Rose, Slyder, Bushman, Warfield, Snyder
groups_list.scope: The Trostle farm (frame house, brick barn with the shell hole, hog pen, summer kitchen), the Rose farm (stone house of 1811, stone barn burned 1910 not in the battle), the Slyder farm (granite house, barn), the Bushman farm (house parts of 1808 and a brick addition of 1860, barn a temporary hospital, a tablet naming a XII Corps hospital at the house: all leads until a local text carries them), the Warfield (James) house and the Snyder farm on the Warfield Ridge, the stone walls P-04, P-05, P-06, P-14, the farm lanes and fences (Warfield), and the Plum Run buildings.
issues: The Rose barn burned in 1910 (not the battle); the NPS and a web source conflict on the cause (basemap note): carry both.
The Trostle summer kitchen footprint lies on the other side of the house from the photograph (photomatch EG-12): do not use the 2023 outline of the kitchen without the check.

groups_list.title: Terrain changes since 1863: quarries, railroad cuts and grading, avenues, rebuilt walls, modern roads, ponds, removed knolls
groups_list.scope: Where the modern elevation model (the 1 m bare-earth DEM the app ground is built from) differs from the ground of July 1863 ACCORDING TO A SOURCE: quarries and excavations, the railroad cut and fills (the cut as of 1863 versus as of today), regrading for parks, avenues and parking (the monument avenues of the GBMA and the War Department, 17 miles by 1896: the avenues are never drawn), rebuilt or rebuilt-on-new-line walls (the NPS walls of 48-52 in. are not the 1863 profile), modern roads and cuts, ponds, drained or filled wetlands, the removal or reshaping of knolls, vista cuttings. Each row says: the feature, the place, the date of the change, the sign and size of the elevation difference only when a source gives it, the tier. The elevation model itself is not edited.

targets.name: Rebuilt walls of Cemetery Ridge, Culp's Hill, Little Round Top
Quarries
targets.basis: lead: the plan names quarry changes (B.9.2 step 2); the pass finds each quarry in a text

targets.name: Railroad cut regrading
targets.basis: plan B.9.2 step 2 (the cut up to 15 ft deep per Wikipedia, a lead)

issues: Do not derive 1863 profiles from the modern rebuilt Culp's Hill, Little Round Top or Cemetery Ridge walls (CLAUDE.md): a rebuilt wall is a `later` row, never a form row.
An elevation difference is a number: it needs a quote that states it, or the row is an open gap.
The terrain pipeline (workstream terrain, plan B.9.2 step 2) owns the DEM and its error model: these rows are its evidence, delivered by request note.
